title: Dear Mount Sinai Health System, I Guess We Are Disputing This Bill In Public?
subtitle: Public shaming of not-for-profit health systems is our civic duty
text:
I went to the dermatologist recently. He was very nice. Excellent bedside manner. I strongly recommend him, as a physician. I was concerned that I might have cancerous lesions. I did not. They were removed. This was not covered by insurance. I agreed to pay the amount it would cost privately, anyway.

However, I did write the following, thanks to the wonderful Al Lewis of Quizzify , on my bill, after red-lining out unbelievable nonsense they would otherwise include. It says this.

“"Superseding other consents, I consent to responsibility (including insurance) for up to 2 times Medicare following receipt of an itemized bill for appropriate treatment coded at the correct Level."

I wrote this on the financial consent documents in pen. I then paid the copay and the $350 upcharge on the removal of skin tags “not covered by insurance”. The following screenshots are presented to formally protest this contractual violation and of course to publicly shame MSSM and encourage everyone to do the same with all hospitals, but especially non-profit hospitals like MSSM which didn’t provide me with the legally mandated patient assistance documents I requested nor make it clear that legally had to in order to justify their non-profit status.

I received this email today:

Let’s follow the charge. By the way, I called that number, and it hung up on me before I could be transferred to a human. Ah, well.

A click-through and ID verification later:

Wait a minute, the amount of money just changed?!?

They seem to really want me to pay the bill. Or set up a payment plan. There is “no protest this bill” option anywhere here…let’s keep clicking.

Another click, another payment plan opportunity. No option to debate the fact that this is wildly inappropriate. Just more options to pay them with interest…not what I’m looking for…let’s look at the details on the bill?

Ok, still, just copays and the $350 I agreed to pay for uncovered services….details please?

It’s at this point that I will be forced to mention, that despite paying $350 for Destruction of Lesions (along with the AMA commission on the awesome branded product that is “CPT code 17110”). It is a little suspicious that a 350 they shook me down for at the time isn’t reflected?

Subscribe now

It is worth noting this bill has changed since I last logged in. The E+M code has been removed? Thus, ChatGPT-4 is on the case. Consider this complaining in public…

Mount Sinai Health System Patient Relations Department One Gustave L. Levy Place, Box 1042 New York, NY 10029

Subject: Formal Complaint Regarding Ignored Consent Language, Billing Issue, and Lack of Information on Patient Assistance Programs

Dear Patient Relations Department,

I am writing to lodge a formal complaint against Mount Sinai Health System for the failure to honor the consent language that I explicitly provided during my recent treatment, billing discrepancies, and the lack of information about patient assistance programs. The ignored consent language is as follows: "Superseding other consents, I consent to responsibility (including insurance) for up to 2 times Medicare following receipt of an itemized bill for appropriate treatment coded at the correct Level."

On January 18th, 2023, I received medical services at your facility for CPT code 17110. I submitted the aforementioned consent to the billing department to ensure that I would only be held responsible for charges up to 2 times the Medicare rate. However, upon receiving the bill for the aforementioned services, I discovered that Mount Sinai Health System failed to adhere to my consent and billed me at a significantly higher rate. Specifically, I was billed $450, of which my insurance paid $252.53, and I paid a $60 copay and an additional $350. Despite these payments, I am still being asked to pay an outstanding balance of $137.

Furthermore, during my visit, I was not provided with any information about patient assistance programs, which, to my understanding, is a violation of IRS regulation 501r.

This oversight has caused me undue financial stress and disappointment in the quality of service provided by your esteemed organization. I expected Mount Sinai Health System to respect my consent, handle billing matters with professionalism and transparency, and inform me about any available patient assistance programs.

In light of the above, I kindly request the following actions to be taken:

• A thorough investigation into the matter to determine why my consent language was ignored and why information about patient assistance programs was not provided.

• An immediate revision of the bill in accordance with the consent language, limiting my responsibility to no more than 2 times the Medicare rate, and adjustment of the outstanding balance accordingly.

• A detailed itemized bill for the appropriate treatment coded at the correct level, as specified in my consent.

• A written apology acknowledging the oversight and assurance that steps will be taken to prevent similar issues in the future.

• Information about any applicable patient assistance programs that I may be eligible for, in compliance with IRS regulation 501r.

I have attached a copy of the original consent form and the billing statement for your reference. Please treat this matter with the urgency it deserves, as the outstanding bill remains a source of significant concern for me. I expect a response within 14 business days, outlining the steps taken to address my concerns and rectify the situation.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

—Owen Scott Muir, M.D.

I expect you will forward this post all appropriate fiduciaries within a 14 day window.
